what_this_is: the scale ladder from organelle to organism, and HOW EACH LEVEL IS REPRESENTED in this project’s files - which is a different question from whether it can be simulated.

rungs.label: organelle
rungs.what: a mitochondrion, the nuclear envelope, a ribosome cluster
rungs.representation_detail: NOTHING. No format here has an organelle. The closest thing is UTMM's mechanics channel, which infers a cell's compliance FROM organelle motion - so organelles enter our data only as the noise source for a measurement of the level above them.
rungs.measured_by: high-frequency intracellular organelle fluctuation (UTMM), as a relative compliance
rungs.what_breaks_without_it: any claim about metabolic capacity, since mitochondrial density is where aerobic power actually comes from, and the registry has aerobic-power laws with no organelle to attach to.

rungs.label: cell
rungs.what: one blastomere: nucleus, cytoplasm, a membrane in contact with neighbours
rungs.representation_detail: THE BEST-REPRESENTED LEVEL, and the only one with a first-class object. A cell carries a centre, a radius, surface area, EXPOSED surface area, curvature, and up to five measurement channels - transcriptome (with an in-situ flag), mechanics, geometry, lineage, signalling. In the worked example: present on 31 of 31 cells, measured on 0 of them.
rungs.measured_by: 3DISS in-situ sequencing and segmentation of a confocal stack
rungs.what_breaks_without_it: nothing downstream - this is the level everything else is built from or reduced to
rungs.mesh: sphere per cell, which is a DEPICTION of shape however good the coordinates are: real blastomeres are flattened against their neighbours

rungs.label: tissue
rungs.what: an epithelium, a mesenchymal condensation, the fin fold - many cells of a kind, acting as one
rungs.representation_detail: NOTHING, and this is the expensive gap. A tissue is not a big cell and not a small organ: it has properties - stiffness, polarity, a boundary - that no individual cell has and that no sum over cells recovers. We can store 400 cells; we cannot store "these 400 are an epithelium".
rungs.what_breaks_without_it: the entire developmental middle. Morphogenesis IS tissue mechanics - folding, convergent extension, condensation - and we have no object for the thing that folds.

rungs.label: organ
rungs.what: a pectoral fin, a jaw, a heart - the thing a design request usually names
rungs.represented_as: a CURIE in an anatomy ontology (UBERON / ZFA), and nothing else
rungs.representation_detail: An organ exists here only as an IDENTIFIER in a graph. UBERON:4000172 is a lepidotrichium; the blueprint graph knows it is part_of a fin, which is part_of the organism. What the graph does NOT carry is any geometry, any material, any size. The one registry law expressible on our traits is about this graph, and reading its `level` field as spatial extent is a substitution the Lean module does not license.
rungs.measured_by: morphometric ratios on the WHOLE ORGANISM, normalised by standard length
rungs.what_breaks_without_it: nothing breaks - which is the problem. The pipeline runs happily while the object the request named has no representation, because the phenotype is carried as a scalar on the animal instead.
rungs.mesh: only inside a whole-organism illustration mesh, never on its own

rungs.label: organism
rungs.what: the whole animal, which is what every phenotype value is actually attached to
rungs.representation_detail: Every morphometric trait we score is a ratio to standard length on the whole animal: body_depth_over_SL, preanal_over_SL, caudal_fin_aspect_ratio. The design scorer works entirely at this level, on ten such ratios. SO A "FIN" PHENOTYPE IS A NUMBER ABOUT A FISH, NOT A NUMBER ABOUT A FIN - and that is precisely why only 1 of 48 theorem-carrying laws is expressible here: a ratio of one specimen to its own length has already divided out the size that most laws are written in.
rungs.measured_by: museum morphometrics; 4,673 held-out specimens complete on the ten traits
rungs.what_breaks_without_it: the scorer, the benchmark, and every verdict the pipeline issues
rungs.mesh: the illustration mesh built by sim-engine/scales/mesh/, marked depicted

coverage.headline: 3 of 5 rungs have any representation; 2 have none.

span.note: organelle to organism. A viewer that shows them at once is lying about one of them.

the_gap.the_claim: two of the five rungs have NO representation at all, and one has only an identifier. The two missing ones - tissue and organ geometry - are where almost every phenotype a design request names actually lives.
the_gap.why_it_is_not_merely_a_todo: the pipeline does not fail when it reaches a level it cannot represent. It carries the phenotype as a scalar on the whole organism instead, and proceeds. So the absence is invisible in every output - a fin ratio looks like a statement about a fin.
the_gap.the_measurable_consequence: only 1 of 48 theorem-carrying registry laws is expressible on the ten organism-level trait ratios, a rate of 2.1%. Most of the registry needs quantities that live at levels we do not carry: two sizes, a mass, a power budget, an area, a stress.
the_gap.what_would_close_it: a tissue object with a boundary and a material, and an organ object with geometry rather than only a CURIE. .life already carries per-cell geometry, which is the raw material for both - a tissue is a labelled set of cells plus a boundary, and nothing stops that being written down.

honesty_note: the cell rung is drawn from 16 real cells in the worked example, whose geometry provenance is "depicted" - a drawing, not a measurement
